Above all, he knew what it was to be American: the American identity needed no definition. Now, in the salad bowl era, the American identity has no definition. The American nationality has been reduced to mere citizenship, the common fabric of American life unraveled to a single thread. On that blank white page of his withered identity, many people write their stories. Red Value Gaming, A New Review Website that in Addition to giving a Score also recommends a Price at which to buy the Game

Hey guys, we, a team of 4 students still in college, are doing a little self promotion here, which we heard was tolerated on this site. Basically due to us being college students we have a very limited budget for everything including games. That unfortunately means that we are unable to buy everything at launch at full price. We also have been burnt a lot by games that reviewed well but had very little content and weren't really worth the $60 price tag.

That is basically how the idea of this review website came to be. We want to be a place for value and budget oriented gamers to check out if a game is really worth its price. This also allows us to decouple value and score, which means we can give a great but short game a better score and vice versa.

The way we decide on the value of the game is a combination of different factors including game length, replayability, quality and repetitiveness. We are very happy to hear any question and feedback for our site. Hope you guys like it and maybe see you around!
What's your position on things like gamergate?

Hey there, we will be focusing our website on reviews and only the most relevant game news like game and feature announcements, release dates and other stuff like that. We would greatly prefer to stay out of all political debates and hope to be able to create a site that focuses on the fun that could be had with games. :)

It's not a question of politics. It's a question of trust.

What's to stop you guys from accepting a deal with a game distributor, matching your recommended buy price and their upcoming sales?

That's a damn good question and one that we will have to think about much more and more carefully in the future. I can definitely say a couple of things though.

Since value is very subjective and different based on everyone's life circumstances, the idea of the website is to get the user to kinda get an idea of our value and apply it to his. Let's say the user usually buys the games at around 80% of the value we state ourselves. Then if we put the value at $50 the user will know he'll be ok buying it at $40. If the user has a value perception of 50% of ours he will know to buy it at $25 . So in this case, if we start predominantly putting the value of games at full price, the user won't be able to correllate to our value anymore and the entire point of the website becomes moot.

We are also looking into creating a second value field based on user submitted scores. While the idea for this feature wasn't made to increase transparency but rather to increase user interaction with the site, you made me realize that it could potentially help to do so. This will take some time though since we have very little time. We might be able to get this feature made some time in summer though, so look out for that!

We will of course be also marking any future sponsored content as being so. We hope this is enough to earn your trust and we will definitely be including this question in an upcoming FAQ!
